author: David Villalon / Maisa
underlying: google/diffusiongemma-26b-a4b-it, BF16; full generation with thinking enabled

speed_block.measured_where: from a Hetzner server in Germany, network included

cost.basis_v11: ESTIMATE: OpenRouter Gemma 3 27B hosted reference $0.09/M in, $0.30/M out x 398 measured input and 413 measured output tokens per attempted decision
cost.basis_hard: ESTIMATE: same hosted reference x 1250 measured input and 1084 measured output tokens per attempted hard decision
cost.basis_final: ESTIMATE: same-size hosted reference x 749 measured input and 690 measured output tokens per attempted decision across all 534, failures included
cost.self_host_sensitivity: Actual serial H200 rental equivalent: $0.846/1,000 decisions at measured 1.015s mean wall time and $3.00/hour; excludes idle/setup time.

endpoint_condition: our GPU (lium.io H200 141 GB), reached over the internet from Germany; serial, one request at a time
footnote: Experimental full-generation path over the same DiffusionGemma checkpoint as djev-dev: thinking was enabled and the model could generate up to 8,192 tokens before returning its distribution. Current djev-dev itself hard-codes enable_thinking=false, diffusion_max_steps=1 and read_only=true, so this is not a switch in its published typed API. It is substantially slower/costlier, and 72/534 requests exhausted the output budget without a parseable distribution; those are failures. Cost uses measured tokens and a same-size hosted reference, not the H200 rental bill.
